Do you have to wait before entering?","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"No. If the roundabout is empty you do not have to wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05"]},"rationale":{"text":"You enter only at a safe gap, and an empty roundabout may be entered without stopping.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F05"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Driving situations: roundabouts","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"How roundabout traffic moves.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]},{"text":"How to enter safely.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"This chapter covers special driving situations, starting with roundabouts. The handbook presents roundabouts as a safer and more efficient way to move traffic, and traffic inside one always circulates counterclockwise. This lesson covers the approach and the entry: reading the overhead lane signs, slowing down, whom you must yield to, and when you may enter. The next lessons cover driving inside and leaving a roundabout, emergency vehicles, bicycles and pedestrians, and two-lane roundabouts. Each rule here comes straight from the handbook's roundabout section, so learn them as a set.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Lanes and direction","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Traffic circulates counterclockwise.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]},{"text":"Overhead signs show your lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Traffic inside a roundabout always circulates counterclockwise. As you approach, look at the overhead signs, because they show which lane to use. Generally, the left lane is for left turns, the right lane is for the next right, and the middle lane is for going straight. So before you reach the roundabout, read the sign, decide where you are going, and move into the lane the sign shows for that direction. The lane you choose on the approach is the lane you keep while you are inside, which is covered in the next lesson. The handbook presents roundabouts as a safer and more efficient way to move traffic, and traffic inside one always circulates counterclockwise.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Yielding on the approach","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow down.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"Yield to pedestrians and bicycles.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"Yield to circulating traffic and semitrucks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"As you approach a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicycles. Before entering, yield to traffic coming from your left that is already in the roundabout, and yield to semitrucks. Put together, the list of road users you yield to before entering a roundabout is pedestrians, bicycles, semitrucks and the traffic on your left that is already circulating. Check each one in turn as you approach: the crosswalk first, then the circulating traffic on your left, then any semitruck, before you decide that it is your turn to go. Before entering a roundabout you yield to pedestrians, bicycles, semitrucks and the traffic on your left that is already circulating.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Entering at a gap","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02","sec07-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Enter only at a safe gap.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02","sec07-F04"]},{"text":"Empty roundabout: no need to wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02","sec07-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Enter only when there is a safe gap in the circulating traffic. If the roundabout is empty, you do not have to wait; you may enter without stopping. So the entry rule depends on what you see. In a busy roundabout, wait for a safe gap after yielding to the traffic on your left and to pedestrians, bicycles and semitrucks. In an empty roundabout, slow down, check the crosswalk and the traffic on your left, and enter. In both cases you have already chosen your lane from the overhead signs before you reach the entry. Enter only when there is a safe gap, and if the roundabout is empty you do not have to wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02","sec07-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Busy or empty","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Busy: wait for a safe gap.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"Empty: enter without stopping.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers believe they must always come to a full stop before entering a roundabout. The handbook says otherwise: a safe gap is needed to enter a busy roundabout, but an empty roundabout may be entered without stopping. The yielding duties still apply either way. You still slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicycles, and you still yield to traffic on your left already in the roundabout and to semitrucks. What changes is only whether you need to wait for a gap, which an empty roundabout does not require. Enter only when there is a safe gap, and if the roundabout is empty you do not have to wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F05","sec07-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the entry rule","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Empty roundabout: wait or go?","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you reach a roundabout and no one is in it. You enter only at a safe gap, and an empty roundabout may be entered without stopping. You still slow down as you approach and yield to any pedestrians and bicycles, and if a vehicle or semitruck appears on your left before you enter, you yield to it and wait for a safe gap. Enter only when there is a safe gap, and if the roundabout is empty you do not have to wait.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R02","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Entering wrap-up","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Counterclockwise; signs pick the lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]},{"text":"Yield, then enter at a safe gap.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up: traffic in a roundabout circulates counterclockwise, and overhead signs on the approach show which lane to use; generally left for left turns, right for the next right, and middle for straight. Once you are inside, the handbook gives three rules about speed and lanes, and one rule about how to leave. Then it covers what to do when an emergency vehicle with its siren on comes near a roundabout. That rule has two parts, one for drivers who have not entered yet and one for drivers who are already inside, and test questions often ask about the difference. By the end of this lesson you will know exactly what to do from the moment you enter until you leave. Inside the roundabout keep your speed low, stay in your lane and never switch lanes.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Inside the roundabout","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Keep your speed low.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Stay in your lane.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Never switch lanes.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Inside the roundabout, keep your speed low and stay in your lane. So the handbook gives one rule for each situation. Before you enter, you stay out and pull over. Once you are in, you keep moving to the next right exit, leave the roundabout, and only then pull over to let the emergency vehicle pass. In short: not yet in, pull over; already in, exit at the next right first.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Outside versus inside","fact_ids":["sec07-R03","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Outside: pull over before entering.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Inside: exit at the next right first.","fact_ids":["sec07-R03","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. The handbook shows a one-lane roundabout and a two-lane roundabout, each with notes about bicyclists and pedestrians. You will learn the choices a bicyclist has at each kind, which way pedestrians look when crossing, and then the rules for two-lane roundabouts: why lane choice is critical, whom you yield to before entering, and which lane to use for turning left, turning right, making a U-turn or going straight through. At a one-lane roundabout a bicyclist may either ride through the roundabout or use the crosswalk.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Bicyclists","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-F14","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"One-lane: ride through or use the crosswalk.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-F14","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Two-lane: take the lane or use the crosswalk.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-F14","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"At a one-lane roundabout, a bicyclist may either ride through the roundabout or use the crosswalk. At a two-lane roundabout, a bicyclist may take the travel lane through it, or leave the roadway and use the crosswalk. So in both kinds of roundabout, a bicyclist may be in the travel lane with you or crossing on foot in the crosswalk. As a driver, expect either. You already yield to bicycles as you approach a roundabout, so watch for bicyclists in the lanes and at the crosswalks before you enter. A bicyclist at a two-lane roundabout may take the travel lane through it or leave the roadway and use the crosswalk.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-F14","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Pedestrians","fact_ids":["sec07-F11","sec07-R05","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"From the curb: look left.","fact_ids":["sec07-F11","sec07-R05","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"From the crosswalk island: look right.","fact_ids":["sec07-F11","sec07-R05","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Pedestrians crossing at a roundabout look left for oncoming traffic from the curb, and they look right once they reach the crosswalk island. As a driver approaching the crosswalk, remember that you yield to pedestrians as you approach a roundabout. A pedestrian may be standing at the curb or waiting on the island in the middle of the crossing, so check both places before you enter or exit the roundabout. As you approach a roundabout, slow down and yield to pedestrians and bicycles.","fact_ids":["sec07-F11","sec07-R05","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Two-lane lane choice","fact_ids":["sec07-F12","sec07-F13","sec07-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lane choice is critical.","fact_ids":["sec07-F12","sec07-F13","sec07-R06"]},{"text":"Left lane: left turns and U-turns.","fact_ids":["sec07-F12","sec07-F13","sec07-R06"]},{"text":"Right lane: right turns.","fact_ids":["sec07-F12","sec07-F13","sec07-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"At a two-lane roundabout your lane choice is critical: choose a lane and yield to traffic in both lanes before you enter. In a two-lane roundabout, use the left lane for left turns and U-turns, and the right lane for right turns. To go straight, follow the pavement markings, arrows or signs. This differs from the general rule from the earlier lesson, where the middle lane is for going straight. A two-lane roundabout has no middle lane, so the markings, arrows or signs tell you which lane continues straight through. A second trap is the straight-through lane. The general roundabout rule puts straight-through traffic in the middle lane, but at a two-lane roundabout you follow the pavement markings, arrows or signs to go straight. So at a two-lane roundabout, check both circulating lanes and read the markings before you choose your lane and enter.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-R06","sec07-F12","sec07-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the straight lane","fact_ids":["sec07-R06","sec07-F13","sec07-F02","sec07-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two-lane roundabout, going straight?","fact_ids":["sec07-R06","sec07-F13","sec07-F02","sec07-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: at a two-lane roundabout you want to go straight. The general rule puts straight-through traffic in the middle lane, but at a two-lane roundabout you follow the markings, arrows or signs to go straight. Left turns and U-turns use the left lane, right turns use the right lane, and before entering you yield to traffic in both circulating lanes, as well as to pedestrians and bicycles.
